easy.def: To stay up and not fall over.
easy.example: I can balance on one foot.

more.def: To keep yourself or an object steady so it does not tip or fall.
more.example: The gymnast balanced on the narrow beam without wobbling.

easy.def: A small animal that flies at night.
easy.example: A bat flew out of the cave.

more.def: A small furry animal with wings that sleeps in the day and flies at night.
more.example: The bat hung upside down from the roof of the cave.

easy.def: A stick you use to hit a ball.
easy.example: She hit the ball with her bat.

more.def: A wooden or metal stick used to hit the ball in games like baseball and cricket.
more.example: He swung the bat and sent the ball over the fence.

easy.def: To hit something, like a ball.
easy.example: The cat likes to bat the toy.

more.def: To hit at something with a bat or with your hand or paw.
more.example: The kitten batted the string back and forth.

easy.def: Very nice to look at or hear.

more.def: Very pleasing to see, hear, or think about.
more.example: The beautiful music made everyone stop and listen.

easy.def: To think that something is true.

more.def: To feel sure that something is true or real.
more.example: She believed her team could win if they worked together.

easy.example: The cat is beneath the table.

more.example: The treasure was buried beneath an old oak tree.

easy.def: A flower on a tree or plant.

more.def: A flower, especially one on a tree that will later grow fruit.
more.example: In spring, the apple trees are covered in white blossoms.

easy.def: To use something that is not yours and then give it back.
easy.example: Can I borrow your red crayon?

more.def: To take and use something that belongs to someone else, planning to return it.
more.example: She borrowed three books from the library and returned them on Friday.

easy.def: A line that shows where a place ends.
easy.example: The fence is the boundary of our yard.

more.def: A line or edge that marks where one area ends and another begins.
more.example: The river forms the boundary between the two countries.

easy.example: The brave girl went down the big slide.

more.def: Willing to do something hard or scary even when you feel afraid.
more.example: It was brave of him to speak in front of the whole school.

easy.example: A cool breeze blew my hair.

more.example: A breeze from the sea kept us cool on the hot beach.

more.def: Giving off or filled with a lot of light; also, strong in color.
more.example: The bright moon lit up the whole field.

easy.def: A group of things tied together.
easy.example: Dad had a bundle of sticks.

more.def: A number of things tied or wrapped together.
more.example: She carried a bundle of newspapers under her arm.

easy.def: A hole in the ground where an animal lives.
easy.example: The rabbit ran into its burrow.

more.def: A hole or tunnel that an animal digs in the ground to live in.
more.example: The fox kept her cubs safe in a burrow under the hill.
